bal-001-tre-3.title: Primary Frequency Response in ERCOT (regional standard)
bal-001-tre-3.todo: ERCOT (Texas RE) entities only. Comment by Nov 5 if applicable.
bal-001-tre-3.what: Texas RE regional revision of the ERCOT primary frequency response standard.

category-2-applicability-revisions.stage: Listed by NERC as requiring modification (Aug 2026)
category-2-applicability-revisions.title: CIP, COM, EOP, FAC, MOD-025, PER, PRC-002/004/005/019/024–027, TOP-001 and others
category-2-applicability-revisions.todo: Category 2 owners should expect a series of new compliance dates and plan program build-out in stages.
category-2-applicability-revisions.what: NERC is revising the applicability of the remaining GO/GOP standards so they cover Category 2 IBRs. Compliance dates come with each revision.

category-2-ibr-registration.title: Non-BES IBRs ≥20 MVA at ≥60 kV registered as GO/GOP
category-2-ibr-registration.todo: Category 2 entities should confirm their registry listing, GADS reporting, and evidence for each standard that already applies.
category-2-ibr-registration.what: Newly registered Category 2 GOs and GOPs must comply with BAL-001-TRE, IRO-010-5, MOD-032, PRC-012-2, PRC-017-1, TOP-003-6.1, VAR-001-5 and VAR-002-4.1 as of May 15, 2026. More standards are being revised to cover Category 2.

cip-002-8-virtualization-set.title: CIP-002-8, CIP-003-10, CIP-004-8, CIP-005-8, CIP-006-7.1, CIP-007-7.1, CIP-008-7.1, CIP-009-7.1, CIP-010-5, CIP-011-4.1, CIP-013-3
cip-002-8-virtualization-set.todo: Every entity should re-check BES Cyber System categorization under CIP-002-8. Low impact: review CIP-002 and CIP-003 changes. Medium and high impact: start the gap assessment now. Early adoption is allowed.
cip-002-8-virtualization-set.todoTx: Applies in full to TO/TOP Control Centers and substations at medium or high impact.
cip-002-8-virtualization-set.what: Revises CIP-002 through CIP-013 (Project 2016-02) so virtual machines, shared infrastructure and new technologies can be secured. Adds new and revised Glossary terms, per-system capability options, and an updated Control Center definition.

cip-003-11.title: Security Management Controls (low impact)
cip-003-11.todo: Inventory low impact sites with routable connectivity, find legacy protocols, and budget for detection capability. Check the Attachment 1 low impact plan against both CIP-003-10 (2028) and CIP-003-11.
cip-003-11.what: Adds low impact controls for assets with external routable connectivity: authenticate remote users, protect credentials in transit (no Telnet or plain FTP), and detect malicious communications in and out of low impact BES Cyber Systems.

cip-003-12-cip-008-8.title: CIP-008 incident reporting threshold
cip-003-12-cip-008-8.todo: Watch the final language before updating incident response plans.
cip-003-12-cip-008-8.what: Revises what counts as a reportable attempt to compromise, which changes when Cyber Security Incidents must be reported.

cip-003-9.title: Security Management Controls (vendor remote access)
cip-003-9.todo: Confirm low impact cyber security plans include the vendor remote access section and the ability to disable access.
cip-003-9.what: Adds low impact controls for vendor electronic remote access: identify, disable, and detect malicious communications.

cip-012-2.title: Communications Between Control Centers
cip-012-2.todo: Applies to entities with Control Centers. Verify the plan covers availability of real-time assessment and monitoring data links.
cip-012-2.what: Extends protection of real-time data between Control Centers to cover availability as well as confidentiality and integrity.

cip-014-4.title: Physical Security
cip-014-4.todoTx: Confirm which facilities meet the CIP-014 criteria, then review the risk assessment, threat evaluation and security plan against the new version.
cip-014-4.what: Revised physical security requirements for transmission stations and substations that meet the CIP-014 applicability criteria.

cip-015-1.title: Internal Network Security Monitoring
cip-015-1.todo: Applies only to control centers with high or medium impact BCS with ERC. Superseded by CIP-015-2 one year later.
cip-015-1.what: Requires INSM inside the ESP for high impact and medium impact BCS with external routable connectivity at Control Centers.

milestones.l: Phase 2a: remaining medium impact BCS with ERC, plus PCAs and supporting systems
Phase 2b: EACMS, PACS and supporting systems for all other medium impact BCS with ERC

cip-015-2.title: Internal Network Security Monitoring (expanded scope)
cip-015-2.todo: Applies only to high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems with external routable connectivity, such as a GOP control center. Scope sensor coverage for EACMS and PACS now.
cip-015-2.todoTx: Applies to TO/TOP Control Centers and substations with medium or high impact BCS with ERC.
cip-015-2.what: Extends INSM beyond the ESP to associated EACMS, PACS, PCAs and supporting systems. Phase 1 covers high and medium impact BCS with ERC at Control Centers. Retires CIP-015-1.

computational-load-sars.title: Load loss in planning and operations studies; event reporting and model validation
computational-load-sars.todoTx: Expect future TPL, FAC and IRO revisions that add computational load loss to planning and operational studies.
computational-load-sars.what: Two SARs: one would require computational load loss, reduction and reconnection to be modeled and studied (TPL, FAC and IRO revisions); the other would require load event reporting and model validation by Computational Load Owners.

eop-004-5.title: Event Reporting
eop-004-5.todo: Update the event reporting Operating Plan, thresholds and contact lists, and train control room staff before the effective date.
eop-004-5.todoTx: Update event reporting procedures and contact lists. Same effective date as for GO/GOP.
eop-004-5.what: Revises the generation-loss reporting thresholds so they capture inverter-based resource events (solar, wind, battery storage) and line up with recent large disturbances.

milestones.l: Superseded by EOP-012-4 (no U.S. requirement changes)

news.t: NERC reminder: extreme cold weather best practices report is available ahead of winter.

eop-012-3.title: Extreme Cold Weather Preparedness and Operations
eop-012-3.todo: Keep CAPs on schedule and submit Generator Cold Weather Constraint declarations through the ERO submittal process.
eop-012-3.what: Cold weather preparedness plans, freeze protection, training, and Corrective Action Plans for units that cannot operate to their extreme cold weather temperature.

eop-012-4.title: Extreme Cold Weather Preparedness and Operations
eop-012-4.todo: No new U.S. obligations. Keep cold weather plans, training and Corrective Action Plans current under EOP-012-3.
eop-012-4.what: Replaces EOP-012-3. Adds a regional variance for Canadian jurisdictions only. No changes to the requirements that apply to U.S. entities.

fac-011-5-top-003-9.stage: Ballots held July 2026; check NERC for results
fac-011-5-top-003-9.title: IBR and DER in operational planning and real-time monitoring (Project 2025-03)
fac-011-5-top-003-9.todo: Indirect for GO/GOP through future TOP data requests.
fac-011-5-top-003-9.todoTx: TOPs: plan for expanded operational assessment and data specification scope.
fac-011-5-top-003-9.what: Order No. 901 revisions that add IBR performance to operational assessments and real-time monitoring and include aggregate DER.

milestones.l: R1 and R7 compliance for existing facilities
R2 through R6 compliance for existing facilities

mod-026-2.title: Verification and Validation of Dynamic Models and Data
mod-026-2.todo: GO: inventory each unit's last MOD-026-1/MOD-027-1 submittal date, since R2 periodic verification runs off it, and schedule IBR EMT model work with your OEM.
mod-026-2.todoTx: TP/PC: set up review of submitted models, including EMT models, within the implementation plan's review windows. TO: verify models for applicable equipment.
mod-026-2.what: Replaces MOD-026-1 and MOD-027-1 with one standard covering synchronous and IBR model verification, including EMT models for IBRs.

mod-032-2.title: Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis
mod-032-2.todo: GO: check models against the Unacceptable Models List and line up MOD-026-2 work so submittals use accepted models. A two-year enforcement abeyance covers good-faith estimated data.
mod-032-2.todoTx: TP/PC: update your data requirements and reporting procedures for the new IBR and DER data. TO: provide modeling data for your equipment. Track the phase-in dates in the implementation plan.
mod-032-2.what: GOs and TOs provide steady-state, dynamic and short-circuit data, now including IBR and DER parameters. Dynamic models must be the MOD-026 accepted models; use of a model on the ERO Unacceptable Models List needs a technical rationale.

prc-024-4.title: Frequency and Voltage Protection Settings (synchronous and Type 1/2 wind)
prc-024-4.todo: Confirm protection settings documentation references PRC-024-4 and that IBR evidence has moved to PRC-029-2.
prc-024-4.what: Now covers synchronous generators, Type 1 and Type 2 wind, and synchronous condensers only. IBRs moved to PRC-029 (now PRC-029-2). PRC-024-3 retired.

milestones.l: 50% of existing BES IBRs compliant with R1–R7

news.t: The 2027 ERO Periodic Data Submittal schedule is posted and now includes PRC-028-1. The Align Create PDS workaround is still needed; NERC says a fix is planned for a future release.

Align 7.8.0 bug: PRC-028-1 is missing from the Create PDS list. Type "PRC-028" in the STD and REQ dropdown.

prc-028-1.title: Disturbance Monitoring and Reporting for Inverter-Based Resources
prc-028-1.todo: Plan recorder installs across the fleet to hit the 50% mark. Report any recording failure in Align within 90 days.
prc-028-1.what: Requires sequence-of-events, fault and dynamic disturbance recording at IBR facilities, with data retention and reporting.

milestones.l: R4 hardware-limitation documentation due (Periodic Data Submittal); staggered by in-service date

news.t: The 2027 ERO Periodic Data Submittal schedule is posted and now includes PRC-029-2. Use it to calendar 2027 submittals.
NERC posted a revised PRC-029-1 RSAW (sub-requirement numbering fix only). Check whether a PRC-029-2 RSAW follows before replacing compliance files.

prc-029-2.title: Frequency and Voltage Ride-through for Inverter-Based Resources
prc-029-2.todo: Repoint procedures and evidence from PRC-029-1 to PRC-029-2. Confirm inverter and plant controller settings meet the ride-through curves. Re-check R4 exemption eligibility under the new in-service and contract-date criteria, and file hardware-limitation documentation in Align by its deadline.
prc-029-2.what: Replaces PRC-029-1, which is retired. Keeps the IBR ride-through curves that replaced PRC-024's IBR provisions, and widens the R4 hardware-limitation exemption to IBRs in service after Oct 1, 2026 if the interconnection agreement was signed by Oct 1, 2026 and the limiting equipment was contracted before Sep 1, 2025. The exemption ends when the limiting hardware is replaced. Adds a limited exemption for VSC-HVDC-connected IBRs with choppers. Operational compliance follows PRC-028-1 disturbance monitoring installation.

prc-030-1.title: Unexpected Inverter-Based Resource Event Mitigation
prc-030-1.todo: Set up a process to detect and review unexpected IBR output changes, with data retention to support analysis.
prc-030-1.what: Requires GOs to identify unexpected changes in IBR output, analyze the cause, and implement a corrective action plan.

project-2026-02.title: Computational Loads: CLO-002-1, CLO-003-1 and FAC-001 / FAC-002 revisions
project-2026-02.todo: GO exposure is limited to the FAC-002 interconnection study revisions, mainly for load co-located at a generating site.
project-2026-02.todoTx: High relevance: these loads connect to transmission. Expect new FAC-001 interconnection requirements and data specification work, with a 6-month clock for data specifications once approved.
project-2026-02.what: New standards for computational loads of 50 MW or more at 100 kV or above, plus new Computational Load Owner and Operator registration. Owners and operators must follow TOP, BA and RC instructions and install recording equipment.

project-2026-03.stage: SAR accepted Oct 21, 2026; comments open through Nov 20
project-2026-03.title: Computational Loads Disturbance Performance
project-2026-03.todo: Low GO/GOP impact today. Watch it if a data center is sited at or near a plant.
project-2026-03.todoTx: Review the SAR and comment by Nov 20 (8:00 p.m. ET) if you have large loads in the interconnection queue. Drafting team nominations close Nov 13.
project-2026-03.what: Proposes voltage and frequency ride-through and post-fault power recovery requirements for large computational loads such as data centers. The SAR also notes that TPs and PCs lack accurate models for these loads.

top-003-7.title: TOP and BA Data and Information Specification and Collection
top-003-7.todo: Check that you have the current TOP/BA data specifications and that your response process is documented.
top-003-7.todoTx: TOPs: confirm the revised specification has been issued to GOs, GOPs, TOs and DPs and that collection is working.
top-003-7.what: Revised data specification standard. Entities that receive a TOP or BA data specification must satisfy it.

top-003-8-iro-010-6.title: Data and Information Specification and Collection
top-003-8-iro-010-6.todo: GO/GOP: expect revised data requests from your TOP, BA and RC ahead of this date, and confirm your plants can supply the IBR data points.
top-003-8-iro-010-6.todoTx: TOPs issue the data specifications: update the specification and the collection process. TOs must meet the specifications they receive.
top-003-8-iro-010-6.what: Order No. 901 revisions. TOPs, BAs and RCs may request IBR and DER performance data. Entities that receive a data specification must provide it.

tpl-008-1.title: Transmission Planning for Extreme Temperature Events
tpl-008-1.todoTx: Confirm the R1 joint-responsibility agreements are in place, then build the benchmark cases and study scope so the first assessment is done by Apr 1, 2030.
tpl-008-1.what: Requires Planning Coordinators and Transmission Planners to assess system performance under extreme heat and cold benchmark events and develop corrective action plans.
